geo.title: What to know
geo.body:
Practice the lessons so far, then check your answers.

Goal: I can solve circle measure problems.

  • 11.1 I can find the perimeter of a regular polygon with trig.
  • 11.2 I can derive and use A = (1/2)aP using the apothem.
  • 11.3 I can explain how inscribed and circumscribed polygon perimeters trap the circumference, and state that pi is irrational, so 3.14 and 22/7 are only approximations.
  • 11.4 I can explain why C/d is the same for every circle (all circles are similar, 8.4) and use C = 2(pi)r and C = (pi)d.
  • 11.5 I can derive A = (pi)r^2 by slicing and rearranging.
  • 11.6 I can find arc length as a fraction of circumference.
  • 11.7 I can find areas of sectors and circular segments.
  • 11.8 I can describe a radian as arc length divided by radius. (Not in 2023 IN Geometry; optional preview of Algebra II.)

slides.title: Practice: 11.7
slides.html: Which is better value: a 12-inch (diameter) pizza for $10 or a 16-inch pizza for $16?
slides.reveal: Area per dollar: 36π/10, about 11.3 sq in; 64π/16, about 12.6 sq in. The 16-inch is better value.

slides.title: Common traps
slides.html:
Watch out for these common mistakes:

  • pi equals 3.14 or 22/7 exactly
  • arc length equals arc measure
  • a sector's area is just a fraction of the circumference
